question: Why is the RBI rethinking India's $250,000 remittance window, and where do the dollars actually go?

theme.label: Economy and public money
readerQuestions: What is the headline economic number?
Is this a total number or a per-person number?
How much of the story is prices, exchange rates, or GDP share?
What does this explain about household life?

plannedCharts.title: Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion in August 2026 after two decades of step-changes
plannedCharts.subtitle: Monthly outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, total and major channels · April 2008 to August 2026 · RBI DBIE Report 19
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows the complete 221-month arc from April 2008 to August 2026 so readers can see how rule changes and tax deadlines shaped the flow.

plannedCharts.title: Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion in FY26; inward private transfers were $155 billion
plannedCharts.subtitle: Selected gross cross-border flows · FY2025-26 · RBI LRS and balance-of-payments tables
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Gives one compact sense of scale before turning to the people and purposes behind LRS.

plannedCharts.title: Education and other travel account for 97.6% of LRS travel
plannedCharts.subtitle: Five monthly LRS travel categories · March to August 2026 · RBI DBIE Report 19
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Uses six full months of RBI's March-August 2026 travel decomposition to test what a Rs 50 lakh sub-limit on business and pilgrimage travel would actually touch.

plannedCharts.title: Two education-related LRS lines totalled $1.05 billion in August 2026
plannedCharts.subtitle: Monthly overseas education remittances: direct Studies Abroad (1.9), Travel for Education (1.6.4), and combined total · Jan 2024 to Aug 2026 · RBI DBIE
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Resolves the apparent drop in India's overseas education spending by combining direct university fee transfers with student travel and card spend.

plannedCharts.title: Capital transfers added $1.03 billion while other LRS purposes fell by $491 million
plannedCharts.subtitle: Contribution to the change in total LRS · April-August 2025 to April-August 2026 · RBI Report 19
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Explains how modest headline growth can coexist with a much larger increase in investment remittances.

plannedCharts.title: Resident investment in foreign equities, deposits, and property has more than doubled since FY22 to $3.93 billion
plannedCharts.subtitle: Annual LRS capital-account outflows by channel, FY2008-09 to FY2025-26 · RBI DBIE Report 19
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Tracks the three pure capital-account channels over eighteen years to show why the RBI is scrutinizing financial outflows.

plannedCharts.title: March takes an outsized share of annual capital transfers
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average monthly share within each channel and financial year · FY2022-23 to FY2025-26 · four complete fiscal years
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Tests the calendar pattern after giving each complete fiscal year equal weight.

plannedCharts.title: After the TCS changes, family transfers were lower while travel and equity flows were higher
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average monthly LRS outflows across four TCS comparison windows; education and medical rates changed again in April 2026 · April 2022 to August 2026 · RBI DBIE Report 19
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Evaluates India's 20% TCS experiment by comparing monthly run-rates before, during, and after the October 2023 tax hike.

plannedCharts.title: Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the $250,000 LRS limit from Rs 1.59 crore in 2015 to Rs 2.38 crore by August 2026
plannedCharts.subtitle: Rupee equivalent of the $250,000 annual LRS limit vs the proposed Rs 50 lakh sub-limit and the TCS-free threshold · June 2015 to August 2026 · RBI DBIE
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows the structural asymmetry between a dollar-denominated remittance cap and rupee-denominated domestic incomes and tax thresholds.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
